description: A leading slash anchors an application route to the current origin, but only one slash does. The silent window.open, axios and redirect calls build ordinary root-relative resource paths. Their near misses begin with // or /\: the first is an RFC 3986 network-path reference and browser URL parsers normalize the second to the same authority-changing shape. The absolute opener is the contrast that already named another origin directly. This corpus keeps the URL fact shared by the opener, SSRF and open-redirect judgements rather than teaching any of them a medplum route name.

expected.note: // begins a network-path reference and the caller supplies its authority
the same network-path reference is external when a browser follows a redirect
/\ is normalized to an authority reference rather than an application path
the backslash spelling crosses the origin when a browser parses the redirect
a //host network-path reference gives another origin access to window.opener
the /\host spelling is the network-path near miss and must remain reportable
an absolute external URL directly hands another origin the opener
